cards.title: Objects hold named values
cards.body: An object stores values under names called keys. Read one with a dot, or with the key in square brackets.

hi.title: Objects naam wali values rakhte hain
hi.body: Object values ko naamon ke neeche store karta hai jinhe keys kehte hain. Ek value dot se padho, ya key ko square brackets mein likh kar.

cards.title: Adding and updating keys
cards.body: Assign to a key to add it, or to change it if it is already there. `?? 0` gives 0 when a key is missing.

hi.title: Keys jodna aur update karna
hi.body: Kisi key ko value assign karo toh woh jud jaati hai, ya pehle se ho toh badal jaati hai. `?? 0` key na ho toh 0 deta hai.

cards.title: Keys in order
cards.body: `Object.keys(obj)` gives an array of the keys, and `.sort()` puts text in alphabetical order.

hi.title: Order mein keys
hi.body: `Object.keys(obj)` keys ka array deta hai, aur `.sort()` text ko alphabetical order mein rakhta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print 36, but prints `undefined`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `ages.key` looks for a key literally named `key`. To use the variable's value, write `ages[key]`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse 36 print karna chahiye, par yeh `undefined` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `ages.key` sach mein `key` naam ki key dhoondta hai. Variable ki value use karni ho toh `ages[key]` likho.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Assigning to an existing key replaces its value.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Pehle se maujood key ko assign karne par uski value badal jaati hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a word in lowercase letters and print how many times each letter appears, one per line as `letter count`, in alphabetical order.
exercise.promptHi: Lowercase letters ka ek word padho aur print karo ki har letter kitni baar aata hai, har line mein `letter count`, alphabetical order mein.
